fixes.explanation: Nothing in the text says that. The complaint from Laban's sons is about wealth and possessions, not about how many hours Jacob puts in with the sheep. They say, “Jacob has taken away all that belonged to our father and built all this wealth at our father’s expense.” (Genesis 31:1) Jacob himself says he served their father with all his strength (Genesis 31:6).

That's the answer. Jacob starts by saying he can see that Laban's attitude toward him has changed. Then he turns it around: “…the God of my father has been with me.” (Genesis 31:5) Rachel and Leah are the ones hearing this out in the field. Jacob puts God right next to the bad news.
Rebekah, Jacob's mother (Genesis 28:5), isn't part of this conversation. Jacob says, “…the God of my father has been with me.” (Genesis 31:5) He's pointing his wives to God, not to a family member.
Esau, Jacob's brother (Genesis 27:11), isn't named in what Jacob tells his wives here. He says, “…the God of my father has been with me.” (Genesis 31:5) The One who has been with him is God.

Three changes and you're just annoyed at payday. Jacob's number is bigger. He says Laban “…has cheated me and changed my wages ten times…” (Genesis 31:7) At ten, you're checking the pay envelope with a magnifying glass.
Fields aren't in this line. Jacob says, “Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock and given them to me.” (Genesis 31:9) His word is livestock, and that's the animals.

Gifts aren't what the angel has his eyes on. He says, “…for I have seen all that Laban has done to you.” (Genesis 31:12) What's been seen is Laban's doing. Nobody in this dream is handing Jacob a receipt for his offerings.

Servants isn't the word they use. Rachel and Leah ask, “Are we not regarded by him as outsiders?” (Genesis 31:15) It's a question about how their father regards them, and I think it stings to ask it out loud. The word they land on is outsiders.
Rivals sounds dramatic, but it isn't their word. They ask, “Are we not regarded by him as outsiders?” (Genesis 31:15) Outsiders is like getting a visitor badge at your own family's front door.

Waiting isn't on their list. Rachel and Leah say, “So do whatever God has told you.” (Genesis 31:16) Nothing about their brothers calming down comes up. Their answer is to go with what God said, and that's it.

Esau, Jacob's brother (Genesis 27:11), isn't named in this passage. The text says Jacob is going “…to his father Isaac in the land in Canaan.” (Genesis 31:18) Isaac is the destination it gives, not Seir.

No cover story about moving the flocks is mentioned. The text says Jacob deceived Laban “…by not telling him that he was running away.” (Genesis 31:20) The thing he kept back was that he was running away.

The Nile is a famous river, but it isn't the one in this verse. The text says Jacob “…crossed the Euphrates, and headed for the hill country of Gilead.” (Genesis 31:21) Camels, kids and a whole herd had to get across that river, and I'd have paid to watch it.
